subject: How to get the vector of gradients in the inner optimization?

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: How to get the vector of gradients in the inner optimization?
parts:
How to access the vector of gradients in the inner optimization?
TMB automatically prints the largest value, which is 2.940199e-09 below:

> obj$gr(opt$par)
iter: 1  mgc: 2.940199e-09 
outer mgc:  0.001119125 
[1] 0.0009655719 0.0011191245 0.0010285343 0.0002173262

The reason I am interested in this is that failing to
get a good gradient in the inner problem is a sign of trouble 
(although in  this particular output there are no problems).
In order to diagnose the problem it helps to have access
to the gradient vector.

messages.author: 90b303eef43fd993
messages.subject: RE: [TMB users] How to get the vector of gradients in the inner optimization?
parts:
Try

obj$env$f(obj$env$last.par, order=1)

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] How to get the vector of gradients in the inner optimization?
parts:
Thanks. That is what I needed. 

In the returned vector the parameters (length 4 in my case) come first,
so those must removed to get the gradient vector for the latent variables only:

obj$env$f(obj$env$last.par, order=1)[-c(1:4)]

messages.author: 90b303eef43fd993
messages.subject: RE: [TMB users] How to get the vector of gradients in the inner optimization?

Right. In general one can use:

obj$env$f(obj$env$last.par, order=1)[obj$env$random]
